sources.entry: claude-code-tools by Prasad Chalasani - Well-crafted toolset for session continuity, featuring skills/commands to avoid compaction and recover context across sessions with cross-agent handoff between Claude Code and Codex CLI. Includes a fast Rust/Tantivy-powered full-text session search (TUI for humans, skill/CLI for agents), tmux-cli skill + command for interacting with scripts and CLI agents, a

summary.one_liner: A collection of CLI tools, skills, agents, hooks, and plugins for boosting productivity with Claude Code and other coding agents, with documentation hosted externally.
summary.what_it_does: The README is a short landing page that points to a full documentation site covering installation, every tool, plugins, and guides. It says skills can be installed with a single npx command, with -s selecting one skill and -g installing for every project. It gives one example, installing the voxtype-install skill. It states that most skills work in any agent while a few are limited to Claude Code and Codex. The metadata adds that the project offers session continuity features that avoid compaction and recover context across sessions, cross-agent handoff between Claude Code and Codex CLI, a Rust/Tantivy full-text session search with a TUI and skill/CLI interface, and a tmux-cli skill and command. These extra details come from the listing description, not the README itself.
use_cases: search past Claude Code session transcripts
hand off work between Claude Code and Codex CLI
drive CLI agents and scripts through tmux
notable: Skills installed with a single npx command; -s picks one skill and -g installs globally for all projects
Cross-agent handoff between Claude Code and Codex CLI
Full-text session search built on Rust and Tantivy, with a TUI for humans and a skill/CLI for agents
tmux-cli skill and command for driving scripts and CLI agents
caveats: Needs Node.js 22.20 or newer for npx
Some skills work only in Claude Code and Codex, not in every agent
Detailed installation and feature documentation lives on an external docs site, not in the README
